title: Arena
summary: Two kings face each other across the board: Frost below, Flame above. Every power is a reveal that you can see and read.
problem: Kings' powers hide in panels today, so the most special part of King Down feels like a setting.
idea: Card-battler grammar at a whisper: two nameplates with the real king portraits, a turn token, your power coin, and a tray of the last moves that folds into one chip. When Flame uses Strike, its coin flips and its card turns over before the Archer moves.

borrows.what: The hero power by the portrait, and the history tray of small tiles. King Down already has kings with powers.
The reveal: a card turns over and names itself before its effect plays.
The turn token that sits with the side to move.
The cause line: the check draws from the Archer over f2 to your king.

options.name: Open tray, 48 px kings
options.summary: The last five moves as painted tiles under the board (phone) or beside it (desktop). The desktop default.

options.name: Folded tray, 32 px kings
options.summary: The tray folds into one chip with the last move; a tap opens it. Small portraits. The phone default.

recommendation: Take Arena for powers and card mode: A on desktop, B on a phone. On a phone the board and the next action come first, and the move tray waits in one chip. The reveal is the one strong beat; everything else stays still.
notes: The phone renders use B and the desktop renders use A, as recommended. The open-tray and whisper states show each option on both sizes.
Look at the check state and the Replay: Flame's coin flips, the Strike card turns over, the Archer travels on an ember trail, and a line shows the check over f2.
Tap or hold any enemy piece to read it. The card shows; nothing moves. Red marks only the squares where the piece can take. A tap on a marked square of your selected piece still plays the move.
Tap the Freeze coin: your own figures fade and the targets come as a wave from your king. Cancel, Escape or a tap on your own piece disarms.
The board never moves: not when a card, a prompt or the result shows.
After Reset you play White against the real Club computer. If it uses Strike, the same reveal plays.
Future: card mode. Cards fan out from under your nameplate and use the same reveal.
Limits: one power pair (Frost Freeze, Flame Strike). The five tray tiles before move 12 come from a scripted opening. No board flip.
Limits: the three end tiles are a simple pick (the last two takes or powers, then the final move), not the key-moment check. In the end state the first two come from the script.
For the lead: the kit tips every fallen king to the right, so a king on the h file falls past the board. This demo tips it left on the g and h files. The kit can do the same for all demos.
